newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drilling rig fleet at all-time low - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drilling rig fleet at all-time low - survey.

text.p: The U.S. drilling rig fleet fell to an all-time low this year despite increased demand from oil and natural gas producers, an industry contractor said Thursday after releasing results of an annual rig survey.

The number of available rigs fell by 80 units this year, leaving the U.S. fleet at an all-time low 1,649 rigs, said Reed Tool Co, a Houston-based unit of oilfield equipment and service company Camco International Inc.
While rig supply was easing, demand from domestic oil and natural gas producers boosted rig utilization rates by nearly 3 percent, with 1,263 rigs considered active, the firm said.

"Since available rigs declined almost 5 percent while active rigs rose, rig utilization improved significantly to 77 percent this year," the highest levels since boom times of the early 1980's, said Alex Newton, Reed Tool president.
Fueled by aggressive drilling in the Gulf of Mexico, offshore rig utilization climbed to 86 percent and land rig utilization rose to 75 percent compared to 70 percent last year, he said.
In the company's annual survey of rig operators, the biggest concern was availability of experienced crews as domestic producers step up exploration and production, he said.
